rule: The github-reviewer marks a toplevel or review candidate by a Codex author (the codex-only mode of reviewer-identity.jq) it skips as noise with its own EYES reaction at step 8, under any reviewer_filter, with no commit or push needed, even in a pass with no fixes
description: `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md` is the canonical source for marking skipped noise. The source pin, in step 4, carries the condition and the obligation in ONE span: a skipped noise candidate on the `toplevel` or `review` surface by Codex, as the `codex-only` mode in `reviewer-identity.jq` defines it, is marked at step 8; dropping the marking, the Codex author condition, the `codex-only` reference or the surface limit turns the suite red. The first consumer pin, in the step-8 `toplevel` / `review` bullet, carries step-4 marked noise as a disposed candidate needing no commit or push, even in a pass with no fixes, joined to the `react-marker.sh` call it runs; dropping the noise case, the no-commit-or-push clause, the no-fixes clause, or separating them from the marker call turns the suite red. The second consumer pin, in `plugin/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/reviewer-identity.jq`, carries the `codex-only` filter definition the rule cites: the `codex` registry entry only, a Bot account per `is_bot`, so the reviewer marks only Codex noise and never a human's or another bot's comment. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these three word sequences exist in these two named files; they claim nothing about meaning and nothing about runtime behavior. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) the pins are whole-file presence pins, not section-scoped; (2) the Codex check is the reviewer's own judgment from the author it reads with the comment, since the normalized candidate record carries no author, so no script enforces it; (3) the registry logins and the body of `is_bot` are not pinned here, and a change to what either accepts that keeps the `codex-only` comment is invisible; (4) the existing `marker-write-failed` fail-closed rule that also covers a failed noise mark is pinned by `tests/policy/safety-react-marker-failclosed.json`, not here; (5) a presence pin cannot assert body-prose absence, so added prose that also marks another bot's noise stays green; (6) the EYES marker is per node, so a marked noise node later edited in place to carry a finding stays handled and is not re-dispatched, a known open defect.

source.pattern: skip noise, marking a `toplevel` or `review` one by Codex (`codex-only` in `reviewer-identity.jq`) at step 8.

consumers.pattern: or step-4 marked noise (no commit or push needed, even with no fixes), run `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/react-marker.sh" "$NODE_ID" "$SURFACE" "$CANDIDATE_URL"`
"codex-only" the `codex` registry entry only (Bot account per is_bot).
